description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic renowned for its rich, creamy tomato-based gravy and tender marinated chicken. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it a comforting and luxurious meal. Our classic recipe guides you to create this restaurant-quality delight right in your own kitchen, promising a truly authentic taste of India.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, lemon juice, and salt to taste. Mix thoroughly to ensure all chicken pieces are well coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or for best results, 2-4 hours to allow the flavors to deeply penetrate the chicken.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once the butter is melted and shimmering, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer. Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken until it is lightly browned on all sides and cooked through, which should take about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until the onions become soft, translucent, and slightly golden, which typically takes about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, and 1 teaspoon garam masala, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Mixture
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes, the soaked cashews (drained), sugar, and a pinch of salt to the pan. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let it cook for 10-15 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully and the tomatoes to cook down. Remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaf from the gravy base.

instructions.title: Blend for Smoothness
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the hot gravy mixture from the pan to a blender. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth to help with blending. Blend the mixture until it is completely smooth and creamy. For an exceptionally silky texture, you may pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on any solids with a spoon to extract all the liquid.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over low heat. Add the previously cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Stir in the heavy cream and the crushed kasuri methi. Simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to warm through and absorb the rich, creamy flavors of the sauce. Taste the Butter Chicken and adjust seasoning with more salt or sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Once the Butter Chicken is perfectly simmered, remove it from the heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and, if desired, a swirl of extra heavy cream for an added touch of richness. Serve your classic Murgh Makhani hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For the most tender chicken, marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight. The yogurt helps to tenderize the meat beautifully.
Do not skip blending the gravy, and for an extra smooth restaurant-quality texture, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.
Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is a signature ingredient for Butter Chicken; crush it between your palms before adding to release its aromatic flavor.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: A Culinary Icon Among Indian Chicken Recipes

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in its native India as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian chicken recipe has transcended borders to become a global phenomenon, celebrated for its rich, creamy tomato gravy and tender, succulent pieces of chicken. It’s a dish that embodies comfort, elegance, and the vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine, making it a staple in restaurants and homes worldwide. If you've ever savored its sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy notes, you know why it holds such a special place in the culinary landscape. For those new to its delights, prepare to embark on a delicious journey into one of India’s most beloved creations.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally meaning "chicken with butter," is a world-renowned Indian curry that originated in Delhi in the 1950s. Its creation is famously attributed to Kundan Lal Gujral at Moti Mahal restaurant, who experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato-based gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was a revelation: a dish with unparalleled depth of flavor, characterized by its velvety smooth texture and a perfect balance of tanginess, sweetness, and mild spice.

The essence of Murgh Makhani lies in two main components: marinated and typically tandoor-cooked (or pan-fried/grilled) chicken, and a luscious, vibrant orange-red gravy. The gravy is a masterpiece in itself, built upon a base of pureed tomatoes, cashews (for creaminess and body), and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, coriander, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Generous amounts of butter and cream are folded in at the end, giving the dish its signature richness and irresistible mouthfeel. It's a dish that appeals to almost everyone, from spice enthusiasts to those who prefer milder flavors, making Butter Chicken a universal crowd-pleaser.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need to create this classic Murgh Makhani at home:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   **Chicken:** 1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces. Thighs are recommended for juiciness.
*   **Yogurt:** 1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt (dahi), for tenderizing.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon, for aromatic depth.
*   **Spices:** 1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color), 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon salt.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1 tablespoon, for brightness.

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   **Butter:** 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, divided.
*   **Oil:** 1 tablespoon vegetable or ghee.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped (optional, some traditional recipes omit this for smoother gravy).
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Tomatoes:** 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes or 6-7 ripe medium tomatoes, pureed.
*   **Cashews:** 1/4 cup raw cashews, soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then pureed with a little water for a smooth paste. These add creaminess without heavy cream.
*   **Spices:** 1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri), 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon sugar (balances acidity), salt to taste.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** 1 teaspoon, crushed between palms – essential for authentic flavor.
*   **Cream:** 1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half), for richness.
*   **Water:** 1/2 cup or as needed to adjust consistency.
*   **Fresh Coriander:** For garnish.

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step

Making Butter Chicken might seem intricate, but breaking it down into manageable steps makes it an enjoyable cooking experience.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well, ensuring all chicken pieces are coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. If using, add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add fresh ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Pour in the crushed or pureed tomatoes. Stir in red chili powder, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and sugar. Season with salt. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the oil starts to separate from the mixture.
5.  **Achieve Smoothness:** Stir in the pureed cashew paste. Cook for another 5 minutes. For an ultra-smooth gravy, transfer the entire mixture to a blender (use caution with hot liquids) and blend until completely smooth. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for a restaurant-quality silky texture. This step is crucial for classic Murgh Makhani.
6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan. Add the cooked chicken pieces and stir to coat them thoroughly. Add about 1/2 cup of water to achieve your desired consistency; the gravy should be thick but pourable. Bring to a gentle simmer.
7.  **Enrich with Cream and Kasoori Methi:** Stir in the heavy cream and the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The authentic Butter Chicken is now ready.
8.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves before serving.

## Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few key tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt and lemon juice tenderize the chicken, while the spices infuse it with flavor. Overnight marination yields the best results.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or very ripe fresh tomatoes. The tomatoes form the backbone of the gravy, so their flavor is paramount.
*   **Blend for Smoothness:** For an authentic, silky smooth gravy, blending the cooked tomato base with cashews is essential. Passing it through a sieve after blending ensures there are no fibrous bits, creating that signature velvety texture.
*   **Don't Overcook Chicken:** Sear the chicken until just cooked through. It will finish cooking in the gravy, preventing it from becoming dry.
*   **Kasoori Methi is a Must:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable for the characteristic aroma and flavor of Murgh Makhani. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste and adjust. Butter Chicken should have a harmonious balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Add a pinch more sugar if tomatoes are too tart, or a touch more chili if you prefer more heat.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, creating a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

*   **Naan Bread:** The ultimate pairing! Warm, fluffy naan (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a light contrast to the creamy curry and helps absorb the flavors.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita or plain yogurt can balance the richness of the Murgh Makhani.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Beverages:** A glass of mango lassi or a light lager can complement the meal wonderfully.

## Butter Chicken Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is a beloved masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to dietary preferences or available ingredients:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas for a delicious vegetarian Murgh Makhani.
*   **Lighter Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute heavy cream with a lighter cream or even coconut milk for a dairy-free alternative. Note that this will alter the traditional flavor profile slightly.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, add green chilies along with the ginger-garlic paste. For less heat, use only Kashmiri chili powder, which primarily provides color.
*   **Cooking Chicken:** If you don't have a tandoor (most home cooks don't!), pan-frying, grilling, or even baking the marinated chicken are excellent alternatives to achieve that slightly charred flavor before adding it to the gravy.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a cashew allergy, you can substitute cashews with blanched almonds or sunflower seeds, or omit them entirely, relying more on cream for richness. The texture will be slightly different but still delicious.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's an experience. Its creamy texture, rich flavors, and comforting warmth have secured its place as one of the most cherished Indian chicken recipes worldwide. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook, mastering this classic Murgh Makhani will bring the authentic taste of India right to your dining table. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight in the magic of Butter Chicken.
